Source: A 57-year-old immigrant from Nigeria presents to the emergency department for sudden, severe pain and swelling in her lower extremity.
The patient has a medical history of obesity, diabetes, bipolar disorder, and tonic-clonic seizures.
Physical exam reveals anasarca and asymmetric lower extremity swelling.
The patient has IV drug and alcohol use disorder and has presented to the ED many times for intoxication.
Her current medications include metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and valproic acid.
She was at a rehabilitation hospital when her symptoms started.
